title: layout-thrashing
description: Learn about layout-thrashing. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Layout thrashing occurs when JavaScript forces the browser to repeatedly recalculate layout and repaint, causing performance degradation. This happens when you read layout information, modify the DOM, then read layout information again in a loop.

The browser rendering pipeline includes style calculation, layout, paint, and composite stages. Forcing layout calculations synchronously disrupts this pipeline and causes repeated expensive recalculations.

data.title: Rendering Pipeline Stages
data.code:
Browser Rendering Pipeline:

1. Parse HTML → DOM Tree
2. Parse CSS → CSSOM Tree
3. Combine DOM + CSSOM → Render Tree
4. Layout (Reflow)
   - Calculate element positions and sizes
   - Most expensive stage
5. Paint
   - Fill pixels with colors
6. Composite
   - Combine layers for display

Forced Layout (Layout Thrashing):
- JavaScript reads layout property
- Browser must perform layout to calculate value
- JavaScript modifies DOM
- JavaScript reads layout property again
- Browser must perform layout again
- Repeat = layout thrashing

Performance Impact:
- Each layout is expensive (10-50ms)
- Layout thrashing = 10-100x slower
- Causes janky animations and scrolling

data.text: Certain JavaScript properties force layout calculations when accessed. These include offset dimensions, scroll positions, and computed styles that depend on layout.

data.title: Layout-Triggering Properties

data.text: The classic layout thrashing pattern involves reading layout properties, modifying the DOM, then reading layout properties again. This causes repeated layout calculations.

data.title: Layout Thrashing Example

data.text: Fix layout thrashing by batching reads and writes. Read all layout properties first, store them, then perform all DOM modifications, then optionally read again if needed.

data.title: Batch Read-Write Pattern
data.content: Optimize by batching reads and writes.

data.text: Use requestAnimationFrame to schedule DOM modifications at optimal times, right before the browser's next paint. This ensures you're working with the most up-to-date layout state.

data.title: requestAnimationFrame Pattern

data.text: Use Chrome DevTools to detect layout thrashing. The Performance tab shows forced layout calculations with red warning indicators.

data.title: DevTools Detection
data.content: Find layout thrashing in Chrome DevTools.
data.code:
Chrome DevTools Layout Thrashing Detection:

1. Open DevTools (F12)
2. Go to Performance tab
3. Click Record
4. Perform actions that might cause layout thrashing
5. Stop recording
6. Look for:
   - Red bars in the timeline (forced layouts)
   - "Layout" events appearing frequently
   - "Recalculate Style" followed by "Layout"

Interpreting Results:
- Frequent layout events = potential thrashing
- Long layout durations = expensive calculations
- Layout in animation frames = poor performance

Common Patterns:
- Read-Read-Write (OK)
- Read-Write-Read (thrashing)
- Write-Write-Read (OK)

data.title: React and Layout Thrashing
data.text: React's virtual DOM helps avoid layout thrashing by batching DOM updates. However, direct DOM manipulation in useEffect or event handlers can still cause thrashing. Prefer React's declarative approach.

items: Batch reads and writes to avoid interleaved read-write-read patterns
Use requestAnimationFrame for animations and DOM modifications
Cache layout property values instead of repeatedly reading them
Avoid querying layout properties in tight loops
Use CSS transforms and opacity for animations (don't trigger layout)
Use DevTools to identify and fix layout thrashing
Prefer CSS over JavaScript for layout when possible
Use will-change to hint which elements will change (use sparingly)

terms.definition: Performance problem caused by repeatedly forcing layout calculations through interleaved read-write operations.
Layout calculation triggered synchronously by JavaScript reading layout properties, disrupting the rendering pipeline.
Browser API that schedules callbacks to run before the next paint, optimal for DOM modifications.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Layout thrashing occurs when interleaved read-write operations force repeated layout calculations
Properties like offsetWidth, getBoundingClientRect, and getComputedStyle force layout
Batch reads together, then batch writes together to avoid thrashing
Use requestAnimationFrame to schedule DOM modifications optimally
Cache layout property values instead of repeatedly reading them
Detect layout thrashing with Chrome DevTools Performance tab
Use CSS transforms for animations to avoid layout recalculation
React's virtual DOM helps but direct DOM manipulation can still cause thrashing
data.takeaway: Layout thrashing is a common performance issue that can be eliminated by batching reads and writes, using requestAnimationFrame, and avoiding layout-triggering properties in loops.
